title: Fiber Made in Space: Hype or Real?
description: A Luxembourg-led team drew about twelve kilometres of ZBLAN optical fibre on the ISS. Space-made step-index fibre showed lower loss and more strength, but the team estimates at best a twofold loss reduction versus a theoretical hundredfold.

beats.vo: Could optical fiber made in orbit beat anything we can make on Earth?

beats.text: Of ZBLAN fiber drawn aboard the ISS
beats.vo: On the space station, one month of drawing produced about eleven point eight kilometers of fiber. Without gravity, fewer crystals form to scatter light. But the team expects at best a twofold loss reduction, because impurities remain the real problem.
Follow for a daily dose of engineering.

caption:
Fiber made in space 🛰️
About 11.8 km of ZBLAN fiber was drawn on the ISS. Microgravity cuts crystal defects, but expected gains are ~2x at best, not the 100x in theory — impurities are the bottleneck. Early results; the ISS retires in 2030.
